newsitem.title: USA: Enron unit says San Juan blast cause unknown.
newsitem.headline: Enron unit says San Juan blast cause unknown.

text.p: A San Juan Gas Co spokeswoman said Thursday that the Enron Corp subsidiary was unable to confirm whether a natural gas leak caused the explosion that killed 20 people and injured 80 in San Juan, Puerto Rico.
Company spokeswoman Diane Bazelides said the explosion occurred inside a six-story building that had no natural gas service or connections.
She said the company has a four-inch (10-centimeter), low-pressure gas line in the street area near the building but that the pipeline was undamaged.

"We cannot verify that this was a gas explosion," Bazelides said in a phone interview. "Our people were on site there this morning, investigating a reported leak, a smell of a gas odor. There were no repairs being made to the line because there was no leak found. Our pipeline that is outside the building in the street is completely intact."
She said the company was working to help the victims and "will conduct a thorough investigation" with Puerto Rican officials.

Four San Juan Gas workers were injured in the blast and remained hospitalized, but none were among the dead, Bezelides said. The company is a subsidiary of Enron America, a unit of Enron Corp, which is headquartered in Houston.
